finding.claim: deleteAccount discards the boolean result of canDelete(), so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws on failure.
finding.source: DELETE /accounts/{id}: the path id and the calling user u (any authenticated low-privilege user, non-owner, non-admin)

trace.note: Entry: deleteAccount(User u, long id) handles DELETE /accounts/{id}
Account loaded by id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, with no throw, return or abort

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct logic, but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) would throw but is not called here. No other auth layer is present in the repo, which contains only this file. The sibling closeAccount (line 29) does enforce the check, which confirms the omission.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (lines 9-11) returns a boolean and does not throw. Its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists in the file.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement, so its boolean is ignored and accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, unlike closeAccount, which calls the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
